maya (docs): Hey team — opened a PR to consolidate SOC2 audit-log retention wording and add localized examples for EU customers. https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1428

maya (docs): Main asks: 1) legal-approved phrasing for data handling/identifiers, 2) Go/Python SDK snippets for export + redaction examples, 3) migration guidance for existing customers switching TTL from 90d -> 365d, and 4) confirm KMS wording.

kevin (security): @maya thanks — quick callouts: don’t state "we keep logs for X" as absolute. Prefer "default retention is 90 days; customers may request extensions via contract". Also add an explicit sentence about encryption and key management.

ash (docs): I can add SDK snippets. Do we want code examples showing export+redaction? Example snippet candidates: curl export, Python SDK call with redaction rules. Will push a small commit.

legal-sr: Suggested phrasing (legal-approved): "Audit logs may contain identifiers and event context necessary for incident investigation. Customers can request longer retention or provide customer-managed keys under their service agreement." Please avoid definitive language like "always" or "forever."

kevin (security): Also add: "Audit exports are encrypted at rest with AES-256; KMS integration for customer-managed keys is supported." Link to security page: https://intra.redwood/security/audit-exports

sam (eng): For migration guide: include a CLI snippet to migrate existing accounts: 
```
redwoodctl audit migrate --from=90d --to=365d --dry-run
```
Also mention a canary rollout: migrate 10% of tenants first and monitor error rates.

maya (docs): Pasting proposed doc snippet (feel free to tweak):

```
Audit log retention and migration

By default, audit logs are retained for 90 days. Enterprise customers may request extended retention as part of their contract. Audit logs may contain identifiers and event context used for operational troubleshooting and security investigations. Exports are encrypted at rest (AES-256) and in transit. Customers can opt into customer-managed keys (KMS) for additional control.

SDK examples

# cURL export
curl -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"start":"2025-01-01","end":"2025-02-01","redaction":{"remove_pii":true}}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/audit/export

# Python SDK
from redwood import AuditClient
client = AuditClient(api_key=os.getenv("REDWOOD_API_KEY"))
resp = client.export(start="2025-01-01", end="2025-02-01", redaction={"remove_pii": True})
print(resp.job_id)
```

Note: migration CLI available in redwoodctl; see migration steps below.
```
redwoodctl audit migrate --from=90d --to=365d
```

```

ash (docs): Nice — I'll push this into the PR and add a short note under "upgrade considerations" about potential increased storage costs and query performance. Also will add localized EU copy: change date formats and mention GDPR-related contact point.

legal-sr: LGTM, small edit: replace "Customers can opt into customer-managed keys (KMS)" with "KMS integration is available upon request and subject to contract terms."

kevin (security): Add a short sentence about retention TTL being configurable per-tenant and the default being 90d. Also add a fallback policy: if a requested retention exceeds an allowed max, we route to legal review.

maya (docs): Thanks — @ash can you own the merge? Targeting Friday EOD for merge after edits and legal sign-off. I'll run the link-check locally once edits are in. :thumbsup:

ash (docs): I’ll take this. Will do the copy edits, add the CLI canary guidance, and ping legal once pushed.

sam (eng): One more ops note — add a recommended monitoring query in console for migration: `error_rate(scope:audit) > 0.5%` during first 48h.

maya (docs): Perfect. Assigning owner: @ash. Timeline: push updates today, legal final sign-off tomorrow, merge by Fri.
